title: Perfect generators from a small triangulated hull
statement: Let C be a pretriangulated category with v-small Hom sets and all v-small coproducts. Let S be a triangulated class and B an essentially v-small replete triangulated subclass of S. Suppose S is perfect: componentwise surjectivity on Hom from all its objects is preserved by v-small coproducts. Suppose every map from an object of S to a v-small coproduct of objects of B factors through some object of B. Let P be contained in B and let Q be the smallest replete triangulated coproduct-closed class containing P, with B contained in Q. Then Q admits a v-small shift-closed perfect family containing representatives of every object of P.

source.place: Krause, Localization theory, Theorem 7.2.1(1)-(3), factorization proof expanded via triangle exactness and evaluation covers.

proof.text: Define R(X) by factorization through B of every map U to X with U in S. Postcomposition with isomorphisms proves repleteness. The shift equivalence transports a factorization to the shifted objects; B and S are shift closed. The zero object factors through the zero object of B.

For a distinguished triangle X to Y to Z and a map U to Y, factor its composite U to Z through Z_0 in B. Complete U to Z_0 to a distinguished triangle with cone D in S. Exactness factors Z_0 to Z to X[1] through D. The assumed factorization for X[1] writes this as D to X_0 to X[1] with X_0 in B.

Take the fiber V in B of Z_0 to D to X_0. Exactness lifts U to Z_0 through V. The commuting square on the last two triangle vertices gives V to Y by complete_distinguished_triangle_morphism_1. The difference from the original U to Y factors through X. Factor that error through another B object and use the biproduct with V. This proves extension closure of R.

For objects X_i in R, evaluate the coproduct indexed by all maps from small representatives of B into X_i. Every map from S into X_i lifts through this cover, by its B factorization and an isomorphism to a representative. Perfectness of S makes the coproduct of the covers surjective on Hom from S.

Flatten the iterated coproduct of covers with sigmaSigmaIso. Its summands belong to B. The small-factorization hypothesis factors any lifted map through B, so R is closed under coproducts. Transfer to arbitrary discrete colimit presentations with Discrete.natIsoFunctor and uniqueness of colimits.

R is localizing and contains P because P is contained in B. Minimality gives Q contained in R. Choose small representatives V_j of B inside Q. Shift closure of B and fullness of the inclusion give the indexed shift isomorphisms, and P contained in B gives representatives of P.

Given maps in Q surjective on Hom from every V_j, factor any map from an object of S to their target through B, replace B by a representative, and lift it. Thus the maps are surjective on Hom from S. Ambient perfectness gives the same for their coproduct, hence for every V_j.

The inclusion of Q is fully faithful and preserves coproducts. Its sigmaComparison is an isomorphism, and commutes with Sigma.map by checking coproduct injections. Transport the ambient lift through the comparison and use map_injective to obtain the required factorization in Q.

theorem perfectFamily_of_small_hull
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Preadditive C] [HasZeroObject C]
    [HasShift C ℤ] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive]
    [Pretriangulated C] [HasCoproducts.{v} C]
    (S B : ObjectProperty C) [S.IsTriangulated]
    [B.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms] [B.IsTriangulated]
    [ObjectProperty.EssentiallySmall.{v} B] (hBS : B ≤ S)
    (P Q : ObjectProperty C) [Q.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms] [Q.IsTriangulated]
    [∀ I : Type v, Q.IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape (Discrete I)]
    (hPB : P ≤ B) (hBQ : B ≤ Q)
    (hminimal : ∀ R : ObjectProperty C, P ≤ R →
      R.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms → R.IsTriangulated →
      (∀ I : Type v, R.IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape (Discrete I)) → Q ≤ R)
    (hperfect : ∀ (I : Type v) (X Y : I → C) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ Y i),
      (∀ i U, S U → Function.Surjective (fun g : U ⟶ X i ↦ g ≫ f i)) →
      ∀ U, S U → Function.Surjective
        (fun g : U ⟶ ∐ X ↦ g ≫ Limits.Sigma.map f))
    (hsmall : ∀ (U : C), S U → ∀ (I : Type v) (Y : I → C), (∀ i, B (Y i)) →
      ∀ f : U ⟶ ∐ Y, ∃ V, B V ∧ ∃ (g : U ⟶ V) (h : V ⟶ ∐ Y), g ≫ h = f) :
    ∃ (J : Type v) (V : J → Q.FullSubcategory),
      (∀ (j : J) (n : ℤ), ∃ k, Nonempty (V k ≅ (V j)⟦n⟧)) ∧
      (∀ X, P X → ∃ j, Nonempty (X ≅ (V j).obj)) ∧
      (∀ (I : Type v) (X Y : I → Q.FullSubcategory) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ Y i),
        (∀ i j, Function.Surjective (fun g : V j ⟶ X i ↦ g ≫ f i)) →
        ∀ j, Function.Surjective (fun g : V j ⟶ ∐ X ↦ g ≫ Limits.Sigma.map f))
